study.article_kind: original computational finite-element and topology-optimization study with a fabrication-feasibility demonstration
study.research_problem: Large mandibular defects require a construct that restores contour and load bearing while leaving space for bone regeneration; autografts, plates, allografts, and xenografts each have donor-site, fixation, function, or strength limitations.
study.exact_gap: The authors identify a lack of comprehensive design and optimization criteria that couple mandibular implant biomechanics with bone-graft mechanobiology across the early, immature, and mature healing states.
study.objective_or_hypothesis: Develop and iteratively optimize a patient-tailored 3D Ti6Al4V lattice-like mandibular implant, using implant von-Mises stress below the 897 MPa yield-strength criterion and bone-graft strain within 0–3000 microstrain as design gates, then demonstrate that the optimized geometry can be fabricated by metal additive manufacturing.
study.study_design: CBCT-derived mandibular reconstructions (figures show Patients 1–4) were mirrored to restore defects and used to build a virtual implant with an internal 5 mm-pore dodecahedral trabecular-like lattice, an external grid-like cortical component, a 2 mm retainer, and a 0.2–0.8 mm strut-diameter gradient. ANSYS FE models used literature material properties and an 800 N maximum-bite loading represented by eight muscle springs at granulation-tissue, immature-bone, and mature-bone stages. Original and locally tuned optimized designs were compared; one optimized Ti6Al4V implant was then selectively laser melted and imaged by SEM. No mechanical, animal, or clinical endpoint was tested.
study.sample_or_model: The geometric source is CBCT data from several mandibular-defect cases (Patients 1–4 are shown, but no analyzed n or statistical replication is specified). The FE assembly contains cortical and cancellous bone, tooth, articular disc, implant, bone-graft material, and screws; all materials are modeled as homogeneous, isotropic, linear elastic. Healing-state graft moduli are 0.2 MPa (granulation tissue), 1000 MPa (immature bone), and 5000 MPa (mature bone), with cortical bone 15,000 MPa, cancellous bone 1500 MPa, and Ti6Al4V 110,000 MPa.
comparators: Original non-optimized versus locally tuned optimized lattice-like implant (S009:C01–S011:C01).
Granulation tissue, immature bone, and mature bone healing-state inputs under the same 800 N maximum-bite loading (S006:C01; S009:C01; S010:C01).
Implant stress and bone-graft strain distributions, including the 897 MPa Ti6Al4V yield and 0–3000 microstrain adaptation gates (S007:C01).
Virtual design feasibility versus a selectively laser-melted Ti6Al4V specimen imaged after heat treatment and surface processing (S008:C01; S012:C01).
method_spine: Acquire 0.4 mm-slice/0.4 mm-pixel CBCT data, segment the mandible, and mirror the healthy side to reconstruct missing anatomy (S003:C01; S004:C01).
Agree the implant envelope with a surgeon, then combine a 5 mm-pore internal dodecahedral lattice, external quadrilateral grid, and a 0.2–0.8 mm graded strut design (S005:C01).
Build the bone-graft/implant/screw/muscle-spring FE model with literature elastic properties and an 800 N worst-case bite force (S006:C01).
Run the original model through three healing-state inputs; tune local distal struts until maximum implant stress and graft-strain criteria are met (S007:C01; S009:C01–S011:C01).
Fabricate the final Ti6Al4V geometry by selective laser melting, heat treatment, sandblasting, grinding/polishing, ultrasonic cleaning, and SEM imaging (S008:C01; S012:C01).

verification: The optimization gate checks that modeled maximum von-Mises stress remains below the cited 897 MPa yield strength and that modeled graft strains occupy the 0–3000 microstrain adaptation range (S007:C01).

No mesh-convergence, code-verification, or independent FE implementation check is reported; the eight-node high-stress explanation invokes possible strut-edge mesh distortion rather than resolving it (S013:C02).
calibration: Material constants, muscle forces, spring stiffnesses, and healing-state moduli are imported from cited literature, not fitted to this patient's mechanics or to an independent experiment (S006:C01).
validation: Selective laser melting and post-processing produced a specimen with SEM images, which verifies fabrication feasibility only; no mechanical strength, fatigue, biological, animal, or clinical validation of the optimized implant is reported (S008:C01; S012:C01).

The Discussion calls the framework validated, but the evidence is internal FE criterion satisfaction plus fabrication of a few cases, not independent validation of stress, strain, regeneration, or clinical performance (S013:C02).
sensitivity: Two iterative stages vary the solid reconstruction and local lattice struts, and three healing-state material inputs show how the selected geometry behaves as graft stiffness changes (S007:C01; S009:C01–S011:C01).
The iteration is a deterministic design sweep rather than uncertainty propagation; sensitivity to mesh, contact, material anisotropy, muscle-force variability, and defect geometry is not quantified.
application_prediction: Stress reduction and the fraction of graft nodes in the selected strain range are FE predictions under one modeled worst-case bite, not observed failure avoidance or new bone formation (S009:C01–S011:C01).

Claims that the construct will promote bone regeneration, restore occlusion, or provide a clinical solution are bounded application hypotheses requiring animal and clinical testing (S013:C02–S014:C01).

primary_outcomes: For the original design, maximum implant von-Mises stress was 1036.30, 739.22, and 594.05 MPa at granulation, immature, and mature-bone inputs; maximum graft strain was 141,790, 13,336, and 8,108 microstrain, respectively (S009:C01).
For the optimized design, maximum implant stress was 697.35, 398.36, and 293.40 MPa and maximum graft strain was 36,896, 9,039, and 5,789 microstrain across the same three stages (S010:C01).

At the early granulation input, the fraction of graft nodes below 3000 microstrain increased from 35.79% in the original design to 93.36% in the optimized design; mature-stage values were 99.95% for the optimized design (S009:C01–S010:C01).

The paper reports a 43.14% average reduction in maximum von-Mises stress after local distal-strut tuning; initial stress concentration was mainly distal, and the optimized stress remained below the cited Ti6Al4V yield criterion in the simulated cases (S011:C01).

The design was manufactured from approximately 40 μm Ti6Al4V powder by SLM, heat treated at 820 °C under argon, surface finished, cleaned, and imaged by SEM; this demonstrates geometric fabrication, not durability or biological function (S012:C01).

The authors note that only a few cases were prepared and that framework repeatability and controllability remain unverified; eight optimized nodes above 500 MPa were attributed to possible edge-mesh distortion rather than further optimization (S013:C02).
study.highest_evidence_level_reached: Conditional FE design prediction with a fabrication-feasibility demonstration; no independent mechanical, fatigue, biological, animal, or clinical validation.

argument_map.central_claim: Within the specified CBCT-based FE model, locally optimizing a biomimetic mandibular lattice can reduce modeled implant stress and move bone-graft strain toward the chosen mechanobiological adaptation range, and the resulting geometry can be additively manufactured; this does not establish implant durability, bone regeneration, or clinical benefit.
data: CBCT-derived mandibular defect geometries and a mirror-reconstructed solid counterpart define the patient-specific envelope (S003:C01–S005:C01).
An 800 N bite-force FE model compares original and optimized lattice struts at granulation, immature, and mature-bone material states (S006:C01–S010:C01).
Stress and graft-strain frequency distributions provide the optimization outputs, while SLM/SEM provides a physical fabrication check (S009:C01–S012:C01).
argument_map.warrant: The FE model can rank the two idealized geometries for the stated loading and assigned material states; the warrant stops at numerical stress/strain because no independent test measures failure, graft healing, or clinical function.
backing: The geometry, healing-state material assumptions, force components, and stress/strain gates are explicitly stated (S005:C01–S007:C01).
The optimized model improves both the implant-stress and graft-strain metrics across the reported stages and remains printable by the described SLM route (S009:C01–S012:C01).
argument_map.qualifier: Interpretation applies to idealized homogeneous linear-elastic FE models, the reported CBCT cases, one 800 N maximum-bite boundary condition, literature graft properties, and the chosen 897 MPa/0–3000 microstrain design criteria.
rebuttals_or_boundaries: The article calls the framework validated and clinically feasible, but fabrication images are not mechanical or biological validation (S001:C01; S012:C01; S013:C02).
No formal mesh convergence is reported; the authors themselves attribute a small high-stress cluster to possible strut-edge mesh distortion (S013:C02).
A literature mechanostat interval and a numerical stress threshold are proxies for regeneration and failure, not measured bone formation or implant fracture (S007:C01; S009:C01–S010:C01).
Repeatability across complex defects, as-built dimensional accuracy, fatigue, infection, osseointegration, and patient outcomes remain open (S013:C02).
argument_map.argument_coherence: moderate for the model-level optimization claim; low_to_moderate for translational and clinical claims

measured: CBCT image acquisition parameters and defect geometries are observed inputs; the packet shows several cases but does not provide a statistical sample analysis (S004:C01–S005:C01).
A Ti6Al4V lattice implant was selectively laser melted, heat treated, finished, cleaned, and imaged by SEM, demonstrating fabrication feasibility (S008:C01; S012:C01).
predicted: Maximum and frequency-distributed implant von-Mises stress and bone-graft strain for original and optimized geometries at three healing-state material inputs (S009:C01–S011:C01).
The conclusion that modeled strains are sufficient to stimulate regeneration and that the implant avoids mechanical failure under the selected load (S010:C01; S014:C01).
inferred: Local distal-strut tuning is inferred to improve load transfer and mechanobiological stimulation because both numerical metrics move favorably, but causality is not independently tested (S011:C01).
The framework is inferred to be clinically adaptable from a few reconstructed cases and one fabricated specimen; repeatability and generalizability are explicitly unresolved (S013:C02).
SEM evidence is inferred to support manufacturability, not as-built mechanical quality, fatigue life, or tissue response (S012:C01).
recommended: Perform mesh convergence, uncertainty and contact/material sensitivity checks, and quantify case-to-case robustness before selecting a design by the stress/strain gates.
Characterize as-built geometry and defects, then run static, fatigue, fixation, corrosion, sterilization, biological, animal, and clinical tests under representative mandibular loading (S013:C02).
Treat the 897 MPa yield and 0–3000 microstrain criteria as design hypotheses and verify their relationship to observed failure and bone formation rather than using them as clinical endpoints.
proxy_to_outcome_bridges: FE von-Mises stress below a literature yield value is not measured implant fracture resistance, fatigue life, or fixation survival.
Modeled graft strain in a mechanostat interval is not histologic bone formation, bone-implant contact, or restored occlusal function.
CBCT/CAD and SEM images do not establish as-built porosity, surface state, sterilization, or biological safety.
A single 800 N maximum-bite simulation and three healing-state inputs do not represent the full cyclic, patient-specific, or long-term mandibular environment.
overclaim_risks: The abstract and conclusion upgrade internal FE criterion satisfaction to sufficient strength, stimulated bone regeneration, and a clinical solution without independent endpoints (S001:C01; S014:C01).
The word validated is stronger than the reported evidence because no external mechanical, animal, or clinical comparison is present (S001:C01; S013:C02).
The 43.14% stress reduction and 93.36% early physiological-strain fraction are model outputs conditional on idealized inputs and should not be presented as measured efficacy (S011:C01).
Fabrication of a specimen may be mistaken for process qualification or as-built quality assurance even though no dimensional or mechanical characterization is reported (S012:C01).

section_moves.move: Narrow the clinical burden of large mandibular defects into a biomimetic design and validation gap.
section_moves.execution: The Introduction contrasts autografts, titanium plates, allografts, and xenografts, then specifies the need to couple cortical/trabecular architecture with mechanical and mechanobiological criteria (S002:C01).
section_moves.transferable_principle: End an implant-design introduction with the exact defect, design variables, comparator, loading/validation level, and endpoint boundary.
section_moves.failure_mode: Do not let a mechanobiological rationale substitute for measured regeneration or clinical function.

section_moves.move: Expose the geometry, healing-state inputs, boundary conditions, and optimization gates before reporting stress maps.
section_moves.execution: CBCT reconstruction, lattice morphology, material constants, muscle-spring loading, and yield/strain criteria are described before the original-versus-optimized comparison (S003:C01–S008:C01).
section_moves.transferable_principle: For a patient-specific FE implant study, state what is reconstructed, assigned from literature, simulated, and physically fabricated before using the term optimal.
section_moves.failure_mode: Presenting planned or assigned manufacturing/material parameters as measured evidence hides the computational boundary.

section_moves.move: Report the complete healing-stage comparator with units and threshold criteria, then separate fabrication from model results.
section_moves.execution: The paper first reports original stress/strain distributions, then optimized values and percentage changes, and only afterward describes SLM fabrication and SEM images (S009:C01–S012:C01).
section_moves.transferable_principle: Keep numerical predictions by state and comparator visible; label a print/SEM step as feasibility rather than validation.
section_moves.failure_mode: A favorable early-stage percentage should not erase the high original strain, mesh caveat, or missing uncertainty.

section_moves.move: Connect stress concentration and mechanobiological strain to a bounded design mechanism while retaining the mesh and reproducibility caveats.
section_moves.execution: The Discussion explains distal stress concentration and local strut tuning, compares the biomimetic lattice with prior implants, then acknowledges few cases and absent animal/clinical verification (S013:C01–S013:C02).
section_moves.transferable_principle: When interpreting an FE optimization, state which response is modeled, which endpoint is proxied, and which next experiment would discriminate the mechanism.
section_moves.failure_mode: Do not convert a strain-adaptation interval into proven osteogenesis or call a framework clinically validated without external evidence.

section_moves.move: Summarize a conditional candidate design and explicitly stop at the FE/fabrication evidence level.
section_moves.execution: The Conclusion repeats the optimized stress/strain rationale and clinical promise without a strong independent-test qualifier (S014:C01).
section_moves.transferable_principle: A conclusion may identify a model-screened implant candidate but should name the missing mechanical, biological, animal, and clinical tests in the same paragraph.
section_moves.failure_mode: Words such as possesses sufficient strength, promotes regeneration, or validated clinical strategy upgrade predictions into demonstrated outcomes.

author_reported: Repeatability and controllability of the framework are not verified; only a few custom cases have been designed and prepared (S013:C02).
The authors request additional clinical studies or animal experiments to evaluate clinical appropriateness (S013:C02).
The Discussion notes a small high-stress cluster that may arise from finite-element strut-edge mesh distortion (S013:C02).
reader_identified: No formal mesh convergence, element-quality report, uncertainty propagation, or independent implementation check is provided.
All materials are homogeneous, isotropic, and linearly elastic; contact, fixation, defect healing, anisotropy, and manufacturing defects are not represented (S006:C01).
The 800 N maximum-bite case and literature muscle springs do not cover cyclic chewing, patient-specific force variation, impact, or long-term fatigue.
Case count, screw allocation, statistical replication, confidence intervals, and as-built dimensional/porosity measurements are not reported clearly.
The mechanostat strain range and Ti6Al4V yield value are imported criteria, not calibrated against observed graft regeneration or implant failure.
likely_bias_direction: Idealized geometry, fixed material values, and deterministic muscle loading likely understate interface, patient, and manufacturing variability.
Selecting local struts until the prespecified thresholds are met favors the optimized model and may overstate robustness outside the modeled cases.
Using graft strain as a regeneration proxy biases the interpretation upward relative to histology, imaging, or functional bone outcomes.
Calling fabrication feasibility validation may favor an optimistic translational reading despite absent mechanical and biological tests.
limitations.scope_boundary: The study supports conditional numerical comparison of original and optimized Ti6Al4V lattice-like mandibular implants under one 800 N bite-force model and three assigned healing-state materials, plus demonstration that a geometry can be SLM fabricated. It does not establish as-built quality, fatigue or fixation life, bone ingrowth, infection resistance, animal response, patient function, or clinical superiority.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Separate an FE optimization gate from independent validation: report stress/strain thresholds as design criteria, fabrication/SEM as feasibility, and mechanical or biological testing as still-required evidence.
writing_capability_candidates.manuscript_use: Methods evidence ledger, Results boundary, and translational Discussion.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: A printed specimen can support manufacturability only when dimensional, mechanical, and biological qualification are separately reported; SEM alone cannot validate those endpoints.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Present optimization results as a state-by-comparator matrix, preserving units, thresholds, negative/high-strain regions, and the distinction between model input and measured outcome.
writing_capability_candidates.manuscript_use: Computational Results tables, design-selection Discussion, and audit of compressed abstracts.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: If an output is a frequency fraction or proxy strain, it must not be rewritten as a measured regeneration rate or clinical success percentage.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Use a validation firewall that labels literature material inputs and mechanostat criteria as assumptions, internal FE checks as verification, and animal/clinical tests as the next discriminating rung.
writing_capability_candidates.manuscript_use: Methods verification/calibration ledger and Discussion limitations.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: Meeting a literature yield or strain interval does not verify mesh behavior, material transferability, fatigue, bone ingrowth, or patient benefit.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: When a model contains unresolved mesh distortion, omit no adverse node, threshold exceedance, or repeatability gap; lower the confidence of the design claim and specify the next test.
writing_capability_candidates.manuscript_use: FE quality audit, Results caveat, and revision of overstrong Conclusions.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: A resolved convergence study can upgrade verification, but an explanatory assertion about mesh distortion is not itself a convergence result.

quality.comparator_fairness: moderate for original-versus-optimized virtual designs; low for generalization across cases
critical_weaknesses: No independent mechanical, biological, animal, or clinical validation; SLM/SEM demonstrates fabrication only.
No formal mesh convergence or uncertainty analysis, with a residual mesh-distortion caveat.
Idealized homogeneous linear-elastic materials, fixed muscle springs, and a single 800 N loading scenario.
Unclear analyzed case count and limited repeatability evidence.
Model stress and mechanostat proxies are promoted to regeneration and clinical claims.
quality.overall_credibility: moderate for conditional FE optimization and fabrication feasibility; low for bone-regeneration, durability, and clinical claims

summary_zh: 这是一项以 CBCT 重建为几何基础的原创计算有限元/拓扑优化研究，并非动物或临床验证。作者把下颌缺损镜像重建为含 5 mm 孔径内置十二面体松质骨样结构、外部网格皮质骨样结构和 0.2–0.8 mm 梯度支杆的 Ti6Al4V 植入体，在 800 N 最大咬合力和肉芽组织、未成熟骨、成熟骨三种文献材料状态下比较原始与局部优化设计。优化后最大 von-Mises 应力约由 1036.30/739.22/594.05 MPa 降至 697.35/398.36/293.40 MPa，早期低于 3000 微应变的骨移植物节点比例由 35.79% 升至 93.36%，并报告平均最大应力下降 43.14%。随后仅用选择性激光熔化、热处理、表面处理和 SEM 图像证明几何可制造性；没有机械、疲劳、网格收敛、组织、动物或临床验证。可迁移的写作能力是把设计门槛、FE 预测、制造可行性和临床推断分层，并保留网格畸变、少量病例和可重复性缺口。
reader_notes: Primary Luna reader read every non-reference packet locator in order: S001:C01 through S012:C01, S013:C01, S013:C02, and S014:C01; the complete heading set contains 15 locators and omissions are none.

Full-text classification confirms original computational FE/topology-optimization research with an additive-manufacturing feasibility demonstration; the cue set's animal, clinical, and biological labels are not completed study arms.
Measured fabrication/SEM evidence was kept separate from predicted stress/strain and inferred regeneration or clinical claims.

Self-review retained the 897 MPa and 0–3000 microstrain criteria, all three healing states, adverse original-design values, the 43.14%/93.36% comparisons, and the unresolved mesh-distortion and repeatability caveats.
